title: Chakras: the energy map, reading the seven levels
h1: How to read the energy map: seven chakras, physics, energy and emotions in the destiny matrix

seo.title: Destiny matrix physics, energy and emotions: how to read the chakras
seo.description: What physics, energy and emotions mean in the chakra table, how to work out its seven rows from a birth date and read the whole energy map on one example.
queries: energy map in the destiny matrix
chakras in the destiny matrix meaning

meaning: The energy map is the chakra table in the destiny matrix: seven rows, three columns, twenty-one arcana and a row of totals. Every number comes from the date of birth. A row sets a theme of life, from the ground under your feet to the meaning that makes your effort worth it. A column puts a question to that theme. Physics is what you do. Energy is what drives you to do it. Emotions are what you feel as you do it. The arcanum in the cell is the answer.

The chakra catalogue helps you get your own table and pick the row you need, and seven separate articles go through each level in detail. This guide is about something else: how to read the table as a whole. How a cell turns into a thought, three cards into one coherent row, and seven rows into a portrait of a person. There is one example throughout: 4 March 1993. The same date is worked through in all seven chakra articles, so you can follow it across the whole site.

paragraphs: Here is the energy map for 4 March 1993. The rows go in reading order, from Muladhara to Sahasrara.

Every cell is read with the same formula: **the row is the theme, the column is the question, the arcanum is the answer.** Take the cell where Anahata meets physics. The theme is closeness, the question is “what do I do when I love someone?”, and the answer is 12, the Hanged Man: stop and look at the situation through the other person’s eyes. The next cell, energy: “what keeps me close to someone?” The answer is 11, Strength: staying close even when feelings run high. Now Vishuddha and emotions: “what do I feel when people answer me?” The answer is 15, the Devil: it is hard to let a conversation go when the answer is not the one you hoped for.

There are three things the table does not show. The numbers are arcanum numbers, not scores: 22 is not “stronger” than 3, and the Sun is not “better” than the Tower. A card’s number cannot tell you that a chakra is empty, closed or weak: for any real date all 21 cells are filled, and the number is not a measure of strength. And no number says anything about your wellbeing. The map describes how you live each theme, not the state of your body.

article_sections.h2: How to work out your energy map: a step-by-step example
paragraphs: The calculator builds the whole table at once. But it is worth working it out by hand at least once: you will see that these are not 21 random numbers but one structure, in which the rows grow out of each other.

One rule covers the whole calculation: **if a sum is greater than 22, add up its digits**, and repeat until you get a number from 1 to 22. 29 → 2 + 9 = 11, 40 → 4, 26 → 8. The number 22 is not reduced: it is the Fool.

**Step 1. The three numbers of the date.** The day is 4. If you were born on the 23rd or later, the day is reduced too: 25 → 7, 31 → 4. The month is 3. The year is the sum of its digits: 1 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 22.
**Step 2. Two more numbers.** The sum of the three: 4 + 3 + 22 = 29 → 11. The centre is all four numbers together: 4 + 3 + 22 + 11 = 40 → 4.
**Step 3. Three anchor rows.** You don’t calculate these; they come ready-made:

ul: **Muladhara**: year and the sum of the three, 22 / 11;

paragraphs: **Step 4. Four rows by addition.** The columns are counted separately: physics is added to physics, energy to energy.

**Step 5. Emotions are the sum of the first two numbers in the row.** Muladhara: 22 + 11 = 33 → 6. Svadhisthana: 8 + 15 = 23 → 5. Manipura: 4 + 4 = 8. Anahata: 12 + 11 = 23 → 5. Vishuddha: 8 + 7 = 15. Ajna: 12 + 10 = 22. Sahasrara: 4 + 3 = 7.

**Step 6. Totals.** Add up each column from top to bottom and reduce the sum. Physics: 22 + 8 + 4 + 12 + 8 + 12 + 4 = 70 → 7. Energy: 11 + 15 + 4 + 11 + 7 + 10 + 3 = 61 → 7. Emotions: 6 + 5 + 8 + 5 + 15 + 22 + 7 = 68 → 14.
Done: this is the very table from the start of the article.

**The energy map is a road through the whole matrix.** On the chart, Sahasrara sits at the very edge, in the outer points of the day and the month (A and B). Ajna, Vishuddha and Anahata are points on the same two rays, each one closer to the centre than the last. Manipura is the centre itself (E). Svadhisthana is the first pair of points past the centre, on the rays of the year and the bottom point, and Muladhara is the outer points of the year and the sum (C and D), at the opposite edge. Reading the table from Muladhara to Sahasrara, you cross the chart from one edge, through the core, to the other.

**The centre goes into five rows out of seven.** Only the two outer rows, Sahasrara and Muladhara, do not depend on it. That is how the formula is built, not proof of anything, but the image is apt: will, desire, heart, voice and understanding gather around one point, while meaning and footing stand at the edges.

**The whole map rests on three numbers.** Day, month and year: nothing else is needed. That is why there are far fewer different tables than dates: the 46,021 days from 1900 to 2025 give only 5,544 versions of the energy map. The table from our example is shared by fourteen dates: 4 and 31 March of 1939, 1948, 1957, 1966, 1975, 1984 and 1993.
**Four quick checks.** If your table was worked out somewhere else and you have doubts about it:

ol: the first number of Sahasrara is your birth day (reduced), and the second is the number of the month;
in Manipura the first two numbers are the same;
in every row the third number is the sum of the first two, reduced if needed;
Svadhisthana energy is one of seven numbers: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 21.

paragraphs: If even one rule fails, the table was worked out by a different method or with a mistake. The most common slip is forgetting to reduce a sum above 22.

article_sections.h2: Seven chakras, seven questions to put to life
paragraphs: The names of the chakras come from the Indian tradition, but in the matrix they are above all seven themes for talking about yourself. Each row has its own article: where it sits in the matrix, how to work it out, what each arcanum means in each column, and which combinations come up most often.

head: Chakra
Theme
What the row asks
rows: what I stand on: home, household, money to live on, my usual rhythm
what I want, and what I do with my desire
how I take on a task and answer for it
how I love, and how I accept care
how I speak, and what I want my words to achieve
how I make sense of what is unclear
what makes my effort worth it

paragraphs: The order of the rows is a path. First comes what gives you a sense of home, then desire, will, closeness, the spoken word, understanding and, finally, meaning. The three lower rows are about your own world: what you stand on, what you want, how you act. Anahata, in the middle, is about meeting another person. The three upper rows are about how you express, understand and make sense of what is happening.

This is an order of questions, not a ladder of merit. Sahasrara is not “higher” than Muladhara in quality. A person with a clear sense of meaning can live for years without solid footing, and the other way round.

There is a quiet arithmetic rhyme in this order, too. Sahasrara is worked out from the day and month alone, so it is the same for everyone who shares your birthday, whatever the year. And the first number of Muladhara is the arcanum of the year, shared by everyone born in the same year as you. Meaning comes from the day; the ground beneath you comes from the year.
If you want to pick one chakra and go straight to its numbers, the chakra catalogue is the easier place to start.

article_sections.h2: Physics, energy and emotions: three questions about one situation
paragraphs: The columns have the same names in all seven rows. The question adapts to the theme of the row, but its core stays the same. The difference is easiest to see in one everyday situation. Let’s take one that almost everyone has been through: doing up a flat.

paragraphs.h3: What physics means in the destiny matrix

paragraphs: Physics is what can be seen from the outside. Who drew up the budget, who was first to pick up a scraper, who argues with the foreman, how the money and the deadlines are organised, what you do when the wrong tiles are delivered. If there were a camera in the flat, your physics is what it would catch.

The name is misleading: this column has nothing to do with school physics or with your physical wellbeing. It is the visible layer of the theme: actions, habits, decisions, the way you handle things, money and time. In Anahata, physics shows what your love looks like in practice. In Vishuddha, it shows your way of speaking. In Muladhara, how you run your household.
The question for physics: **what do I do?**

Energy is what starts the engine, and what makes it stall. Why did you take on the renovation in the first place: did you want order, beauty, a new chapter, more comfort for your parents? Why did you see it through when half the crew vanished? And what drains you fastest: uncertainty, other people’s decisions, repetitive work?

No camera can film energy; you have to ask about it: “why?” Two people can paint walls the same way (their physics is the same) for completely different reasons. One of them cannot live in a mess. For the other, what matters is that the decision was their own.
The question for energy: **what pushes me to do this, and what gives me strength?**

Emotions are what you would write in your diary in the evening. Relief when the last wall is done. Annoyance when the tiles turn out to be the wrong colour. The thrill of the first day and the gloom of the skirting-board stage. This is your inner response to what is happening.

The third number in a row does not come from a separate point of the matrix: it is the sum of the first two. You can see this clearly in life: what you feel grows out of what you did and why. Theatre people will recognise the principle. In his later years Stanislavski arrived at the “method of physical actions”: a feeling cannot be played on demand; it arises by itself when the actor acts truthfully towards a clear objective. This is a rhyme, not a justification of the method, but it makes the main point easy to remember: in the table, emotions stand where the action meets the motive.
The question for emotions: **what do I feel while I’m doing it?**
Now the key point. The same card answers different questions in different columns, so it reads differently too. Here are two arcana from our example, in the same renovation.

head: 4 · The Emperor
22 · The Fool
rows: I draw up a budget and a schedule, and decide who is responsible for what
I start the very first evening: the wallpaper is stripped, and there is no plan yet
I want the job to have someone in charge and a clear order; when things are decided any old how, my strength drains away
I want things to be different from before; my interest lasts as long as there is something new
calm while the plan holds; irritation when a wall gets moved without me
the thrill and lightness of the start; boredom when it gets to the skirting boards

paragraphs: The Emperor in physics and the Emperor in energy are not one quality repeated twice. In physics, order is a way of acting. In energy, it is the condition without which you don’t feel like acting at all. That is why the description of an arcanum cannot be copied into every cell where it appears.

The column changes the question, and the row changes the scene. In Sahasrara physics the same Emperor gives an idea its shape; in Manipura physics he organises the work and sees it through. One card, different ways of showing up.

paragraphs.h3: Cheat sheet: the 21 questions of the energy map

paragraphs: Write out the questions for every cell and you get a questionnaire for the whole table. Plug your own cards into it.

head: Chakra
Physics: what I do
Energy: what drives me
Emotions: what I feel
rows: how I run my household, and what I do when my footing gets shaky
what gives me a sense of security
when I feel calm, and what throws me off balance
what I do with my desire
how I take on a task
what gives me the strength to keep going
how I take success, refusal and other people’s judgement
what I do when I love
what keeps me close to someone
how I speak when there is no time to choose my words
what I want from a conversation
what I feel when people answer me or say nothing
how I make sense of what is unclear
what I feel at the edge of the known
how my values show in what I do
what I rely on when choosing my path
how it feels to go my own way

article_sections.h2: How to read one chakra: three cards, one thought
paragraphs: The reference table in each chakra article gives the meaning of any card in any column. But three meanings side by side are not yet a reading. “The Fool: living light. Strength: gently taming worry. The Lovers: calm beside your people.” That is Muladhara 22 / 11 / 6 from our example, and what it all means together is still unclear. The row has to be put together. Here is how.

**1. Ask the row its question.** Muladhara is support: what do I stand on? **2. Answer in three voices.** What I do: I live light, with no excess baggage, ready to move and change the way I live (the Fool). What holds me: when the familiar order falls apart, I don’t rush about but calm my worry (Strength). What I feel: I’m at ease wherever my person is beside me (the Lovers).

**3. Find where the cards argue and where they support each other.** The Fool lives without a cushion, and that is unsettling: at first glance, the footing looks shaky. But Strength doesn’t fight the Fool’s lightness; it makes it bearable. The worry comes, but it doesn’t take over. The Lovers show where the calm comes from: someone close is beside you.

**4. Put it into one thought you can recognise in your life.** In the full reading, the thought for this row is: **“Your foundation isn’t a stockpile but calm and closeness, and you carry both with you.”** All three cards are at work in it, and none of them can be left out.

**5. Find the difficulty in the same logic.** A foundation like this turns fragile when everything rests on one point. There is no cushion, and an argument about the washing-up feels as if the whole home were shaking. The difficulty is not a separate “minus” of the card but the same picture turned the other way round.

Look at the third number. The Lovers are 22 + 11, reduced to six. And in the reading, calm really does appear where living light meets the ability to tame worry. The arithmetic does not prove this, but in any row it is handy to read emotions as the place where physics and energy meet.

And one last check, the most useful one: **swap one card, and the thought should change.** Put the Emperor in place of the Fool, and the row becomes 4 / 11 / 15: instead of a foundation you can take with you, you get one you build and hold on to. If your wording fits any three cards, you are reading generalities, not the row.

A finished row in the full reading looks like this: the heading “A foundation you can take with you”, under it the three cards with captions on the role of each (“Living light”, “Gently taming worry”, “Calm beside your people”), and three paragraphs that go through the same five steps, only now as connected text.

article_sections.h2: How to read the whole map: from rows to a portrait
paragraphs: Seven rows are not seven separate character traits. They are one life seen from seven sides. Three moves are enough to put them together.

paragraphs.h3: Move one: read from the bottom up as a single story

paragraphs: First put each row together into one thought, as in the section above. For 4 March 1993, these are the titles of the seven blocks of the full reading:

head: Chakra
Row
Main thought
rows: A foundation you can take with you
Striking a deal with your own desire
Taking ownership and expecting fair credit
Riding out their storm, keeping the bond
Steering a conversation to a clear decision
Finding a way out where there was a dead end
Making something you recognise yourself in

paragraphs: Read them in order and a story emerges. This person carries their home with them: calm, and the people close to them. They don’t fight a strong desire; they strike a deal with it. They answer for their own work and expect fair credit. Around them, someone else’s storm doesn’t break the bond. They steer a conversation to a decision. They look for another move where everyone else is stuck. And they want to be the author of whatever they put themselves into.

paragraphs.h3: Move two: find the recurring cards

paragraphs: The 21 cells of our table hold only 11 different arcana. That is quite normal: an energy map holds just under 13 different cards on average, and for 93% of dates at least one card appears in the table three times or more. A recurring card is a way of acting that meets you in different areas of life, each time in a new role.

head: Arcanum
Where it stands
How it sounds in each place
rows: Svadhisthana physics, Vishuddha physics, Manipura emotions
pleasure in fair measure · weighing every word · keeping a fair tally
Sahasrara physics, Manipura physics and energy
giving an idea its shape · organising and seeing it through · making your own decisions
the hold of attraction · attachment to the answer
seeing it from the other side · seeing through the other’s eyes

paragraphs: There are other repeats too. Strength appears twice in energy: both at home and in closeness, what holds you is the ability to ride out strong feelings, both your own worry and someone else’s storm. The Hierophant appears twice in emotions: you are at ease when you are in tune with yourself and with shared values. The Fool opens up both your footing and your understanding. The Chariot sits in the aim of a conversation and in the feeling of moving forward.

The most striking pair here is Strength and the Devil. In Waite, both cards are built around a chain. On the Devil, a man and a woman are chained at the foot of an altar, and Waite calls this “the chain and fatality of the material life”, though he adds that “he who is exalted above them is not to be their master for ever”. On Strength, a woman leads a lion on a chain of flowers, and Waite reads that chain as “the sweet yoke and the light burden” of a law “taken into the heart of hearts”. In our map the two chains sit in different rows. The iron one holds you: desire, and the answer you need to hear. The one of flowers is in your own hands: with it you calm your worry and ride out someone else’s storm.

The second pair is the Emperor and the Hanged Man. Three times the Emperor says “keep it in hand”: the idea, the work, the decision. Twice the Hanged Man says the opposite: stop for a while and look from the other side. In Waite, the Hanged Man suggests “life in suspension, but life and not death”.

paragraphs.h3: Move three: put the difficulties together

paragraphs: In the full reading, the third paragraph of each row is the difficulty that grows out of the same strength. Write them out side by side, and a common thread shows:

ul: **Svadhisthana:** every joy has to be earned first, and pleasure turns into a ledger of debts;
**Manipura:** the assessment missed the point, and while the work moves on, inside you the case is still being heard;
**Anahata:** your own things keep being put off, and care becomes a duty done by the rulebook: everything is done properly, yet there is less and less warmth;
**Vishuddha:** the conversation turns into a contest to be proven right, and someone else’s refusal holds you like a chain.

paragraphs: Four different scenes, one movement: everything has to add up, by the rules and by the tally. Joy has to be earned, credit has to match the effort, care has to fit the form, and an argument has to end with you proven right. And behind the tally you lose what it was kept for: the pleasure, the next step, the warmth, the trust. Justice stands in three of these rows, the Hierophant in two. And the map itself suggests a counterweight: Strength in energy holds a strong feeling gently, without crushing it, and the Hanged Man offers to let go for a minute and look at it differently.

The difficulties of Muladhara, Ajna and Sahasrara are about something else: a foundation that rests on a single bond, a new explanation that never gets the chance to meet experience, and a goal that eclipses what has already been achieved. A common thread does not have to run through all seven rows. Force it, and the portrait comes out beautiful and wrong.

Together, the three moves add up to a portrait: **someone who wants to be the author of their own life, and the main question of their map is how to hold the scales without letting them become a chain of iron.**

This is not a verdict, and not the only possible way to put it together. Another reader may place the emphasis differently, but any conclusion has to rest on the cards and their roles. And it is tested by life: if you don’t recognise the portrait, don’t bend events to fit it. Go back to the rows and see where the reading drifted away from the cards.

paragraphs.h3: One card twice in one row

paragraphs: Manipura always has a repeat: physics and energy both come from the same centre, so 4 / 4 / 8 and 9 / 9 / 18 are ordinary rows. In the other chakras the first two numbers match for 3–9% of dates. A repeat like this is always read the same way: one card in two roles, in the action and in the motive. It is not “double strength”. Remember the Emperor from the renovation: order as a way of acting, and order as the condition without which you don’t want to act at all.

A recurring card is read in each row separately, and then you look at what the readings have in common. Some of these repeats follow directly from the formula: the rows are neighbours in the calculation. Anahata comes from Vishuddha, Ajna from Sahasrara and Vishuddha, Svadhisthana from Muladhara. In our example, 12 stands in the physics of both Ajna and Anahata because the arcanum of the day matched the centre: both equal 4, and 4 + 8 = 8 + 4. This happens for roughly one date in fifteen. The formula explains where the card came from, but it does not cancel the card’s meaning in each row.

The extreme case shows this best. For people born on 9 September 1989 or 1998, the whole table consists of two cards: the Hermit (9) and the Moon (18). Since 1900 there have been 42 such dates, all of them in September, on the 9th, 18th or 27th. The Hermit appears here twelve times, the Moon nine. But this is not “a twelvefold Hermit”. It is one question, how to find your own light at dusk, which life asks on seven different levels. Here are the row titles for 9 September 1998 in the full reading:

head: Chakra
Row
Main thought
rows: Working it out yourself when there’s fog ahead
Get to know your shadow in safe darkness
Walking through dusk with your own lantern
Speaking quietly about what matters most
Looking into the haze until it becomes a thought
Seeking meaning where few have walked

paragraphs: Five identical rows, and five different thoughts. The row sets the scene, and the same pair of cards plays a different part in each one.

paragraphs.h3: The same numbers in other sections of the matrix

paragraphs: The energy map is built from the same points as the whole matrix. That is why the numbers in the table also turn up in other sections of the reading:

head: Energy map cell
Where else this number stands
rows: the birth day arcanum, the calling card
three points of the talent line
the arcanum of the year, the material task
the karmic task, which is also the root of the karmic tail
the entry point of the money line
the entry point of the relationship line and the karmic tail

paragraphs: If the same number meets you in three sections, it is not a sign from fate but one and the same point. The chakra table looks at it from its own angle. In the section on character, the birth month is the spiritual task; in Sahasrara, it is what you rely on when choosing your path.

paragraphs.h3: The Total row: the overall energy field

paragraphs: Below the table there are three more numbers: the column totals. Each column is added up from top to bottom and reduced: in our case 70 → 7, 61 → 7 and 68 → 14. This row is called the overall energy field. It is not an eighth chakra but the shared tone in which all seven levels sound. The physics total is the general rhythm of your affairs: how you take on tasks in general, and how you handle time and things. The energy total is where your strength comes from overall, and where it goes. The emotions total is your general response to what happens.

Two caveats. The totals are arcanum numbers too, not percentages, and 7 is not “two units of energy” more than 5. Besides, the totals have their own arithmetic: unlike in a row, the third number here does not have to be the sum of the first two. For 4 March 1993 it does match (7 + 7 = 14), but that happens for only about a third of dates. There are 363 possible total triples in all. How to read them, and how the energy field differs from the individual chakras, is covered in detail in “The overall energy field in the destiny matrix”.

This article is enough to read your table on your own: work it out, ask each cell its question, put the rows together, find the recurring cards. The reference tables in the seven chakra articles give the meaning of any card in any column.

What no reference can give you is a ready-made text about your three cards in your row. Strength next to the Hanged Man sounds different from Strength next to the Fool. And the same triple changes its meaning with the chakra. The row 12 / 11 / 5 in Anahata is “Riding out their storm, keeping the bond”, in Vishuddha “Turning an outburst into a rule for all”, and in Sahasrara “Quiet loyalty to something bigger than you”.
**Free and with no sign-up**, straight after you enter a date:

ul: the whole matrix and the “Chakras and your arcana” table: 21 arcana with their names, plus the Total row;
the “Where the numbers come from” note: which points each row is taken from, and how each sum is reduced;
two sections of the reading: “Character and personal qualities” and “The centre and the inner points”;
this guide and the seven chakra articles, with reference tables for every arcanum.

paragraphs: **The full reading** includes the “Chakra energy map” section: seven blocks, from Muladhara to Sahasrara. Each block has:

ul: **a heading**: the main thought of your row;
**three captions**: the role each card plays in your particular combination;
**three paragraphs**: the theme of the chakra and what each card brings to it; the whole picture, with a recognisable example from life; and the difficulty that grows out of the same strength.

paragraphs: The texts are written separately for every row that occurs in real dates, and there are almost two thousand of them. This is not a patchwork of dictionary meanings: every heading you have seen in this article comes from there. The chakra section is part of the full reading, together with the other sections of the matrix, 20 in all. One payment, no subscription and no repeat charges.

What the full reading does not do: it does not predict events, does not rate the “strength” of your chakras and says nothing about health. It is a symbolic portrait for you to check against your own experience.

Start with your own table: the calculation form is near the top of the article, and the numbers appear straight away. Pick the row that feels closest to you right now and put it together yourself using the five steps. And when you want to see the whole map as connected text, the readings of all seven rows are waiting in the full reading.

article_sections.h2: What this guide is based on

ul: **Calculation**: the classic destiny matrix of Natalia Ladini, with points A–T. Sahasrara is A and B; Ajna is A + J and B + K; Vishuddha is J = A + E and K = B + E; Anahata is J + E and K + E; Manipura is E twice; Svadhisthana is L = C + E and M = D + E; Muladhara is C and D. Emotions are the sum of the first two numbers in the row; the totals are the reduced sums of the columns. Any sum above 22 is reduced by adding up its digits. The example and every number in the article have been checked against the site’s calculator, and the statistics cover all 46,021 dates from 1900 to 2025.

**Card meanings**: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, 1922 reprint), and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Waite is quoted in his original wording. Wen has a seven-chakra spread (chapter 14), but in it each chakra gets a single drawn card, not three columns.
**The columns, the links between cards and the combination texts**: the author’s interpretation. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the destiny matrix.
The destiny matrix is an esoteric model for self-reflection, with no scientific evidence behind it. It is not a forecast, and not advice about your wellbeing, money or relationships.

faq.q: What does physics mean in the destiny matrix?
faq.a: Physics is the first column of the chakra table. It answers the question “what do I do?”: how the theme of the row shows in your actions and habits, and in the way you handle things, money and time. In Anahata it is what your love looks like in practice; in Vishuddha, your way of speaking. The column has nothing to do with your physical wellbeing or the state of your body.

faq.q: What do emotions mean in the destiny matrix?
faq.a: Emotions are the third column: what you feel within the theme of the row. This number is not taken from a separate point of the matrix; it is the sum of physics and energy, reduced to 1–22. So it is handy to read it as a response born of an action and a motive. In Anahata, 12 + 11 = 23 → 5: the Hierophant in emotions, trust in shared values.

faq.q: Why is “energy” the name of a column and of any arcanum?
faq.a: In the language of the destiny matrix, any arcanum is often called an “energy”: “energy 5”, “the energy of the year”. In the chakra table the word is the name of the middle column, meaning the motive and the source of strength. To avoid mix-ups, say “the arcanum in the energy column of Anahata”. For arcana in general, see “Energies in the destiny matrix”.

faq.q: Which chakra should I start reading from?
faq.a: For a full reading, start from Muladhara and go up: that way the rows add up to a story. If you have a specific question, start from the row that matches it. A difficult conversation: Vishuddha. A relationship: Anahata. A decision about a project: Manipura. A move or a change of job: Muladhara and Sahasrara. Don’t pick a row by the smallest or the largest number: the size of the number means nothing.

faq.q: What does the Total row under the table mean?
faq.a: These are the column totals: each column is added up and reduced to 1–22. The result is three arcana: the general rhythm of your affairs, the general source of your strength and your general emotional response. This row is called the overall energy field. It is not an eighth chakra, and not a percentage of “charge”. There is more in the article on the overall energy field.

faq.q: What does it mean if numbers repeat in the table?
faq.a: Nothing to worry about. For 93% of dates some card appears in the table three times or more, and Manipura always has a repeat. A repeat is one card in different roles, not an amplified quality. Read it in each cell separately, then look at what the readings have in common: that is how you find the themes the card carries through the map.

faq.q: Why do a friend and I have the same chakras?
faq.a: The table depends on only three numbers: the reduced day, the month and the reduced year. That is why the 46,021 dates from 1900 to 2025 give only 5,544 different energy maps. For example, 4 and 31 March of the same year share one table, and so do those days in years with the same year arcanum: for 1984 and 1993 it is 22. Gender plays no part in the calculation.

faq.q: Is this the same table as the “health map”?
faq.a: Yes, some calculators call these seven rows a health map. Here they are read as a map of life themes: the numbers describe ways of acting, motives and experiences, not the state of the body. Questions about how you feel physically belong with a qualified specialist, not with the arcana.

faq.q: How is the energy map different from a chakra analysis in percentages?
faq.a: They are different methods. A chakra analysis by date of birth gives percentages or small numbers from its own formula, while the destiny matrix puts one of the 22 arcana into each cell. Comparing “78%” with the Emperor makes no sense, and readings cannot be carried over from one system to the other.

faq.q: Why did another calculator give me different numbers?
faq.a: There are usually three reasons. The first is the reduction rule: here the digits are added up (23 → 5), while some calculators subtract 22 (23 → 1), and the tables then hardly ever match. The second is the order: rows sometimes run from the top down, and the columns come in a different sequence. The third is the numbering: the destiny matrix uses the old Marseille order, where 8 is Justice, 11 is Strength and 22 is the Fool (Waite numbers it 0). Waite and many Tarot books swap Strength and Justice, so match readings by the card’s name, not its number. The four rules from the calculation section will help you check your table.
